note: Track open-chords, step 3 (a mix): Em, Am, E, A and D together. The shapes from memory on chord-shapes, minor next to major on a strum-along, then ten bars in which every pair of the five chords meets once, one strum a bar. Each strum-along carries its pattern, the tempo is moves (the open shapes keep their key), and each block has one extra line: a feel, what to listen for, what to do when a change comes late.

exercise.title: Five open chords, any two in a row
exercise.why: Every change between two chords is its own move, so playing the five chords in an order where each one meets every other once shows you which changes are still slow.

cells.text:
Press a chord box below to hear it. Fret each of the five chords in turn, and look at its chord box only after your fingers are down.
Practice until every shape lands without a look.

Press Play below to start the metronome. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play: strum down once on beat 1, then use the rest of the bar to move to the next chord.
When Em changes to E and Am changes to A, listen for the one note that goes up.

Press Play below to start the metronome. The ten bars hold the five chords in an order where every chord meets each of the others once: strum down once on beat 1, then move.
If a change comes late, keep counting and catch the next beat 1.
